why: User wanted pub-specific links to open a focused shadow-box style panel on top.
implications: /dashboard/cro UX differs from home CRO; modal shares same metrics component.

what: ExecutiveGroupOverview CEO split: Net Revenue → Gross split + one-line note Publishers+Mula=gross (rollup). MulaRevenueChart: Tooltip cursor={false} (removes full-height grey axis band on hover); Bar background={false}.

what: metrics.js: overlayNetworkMulaOnMonthlyTotals + buildMonthlyTotalsFromPublisherRows(publishers, network) replaces mulaRev per month from Network tab when that month exists; else keeps publisher sum. GET /api/live passes monthlyNetwork.rows. buildKpis meta.monthlyChartsSource updated. MulaRevenueChart subtitle reflects Network-primary + fallback. Removed CEO/CRO NetworkRevenueSplit footnotes and ExecutiveGroupOverview CEO mismatch blurb.
why: User wanted one consistent Mula $ for a month across CEO headline and Mula-by-month chart.
implications: sync-rollup-lib copies need second arg to buildMonthlyTotalsFromPublisherRows where mirrored; publisher-tab Mula sum still used for lifetime tables and QA publishers_sum_vs_network.

title: COO panel: network-first widgets + publisher section
what: CooPersonaPanel: Network block — weekly network revenue TrendChart + span narrative (Are we growing?), MoM trio card (revenue, PVs, blended RPM vs last month), Channel mix + Publisher mix strips (publisherMoM + sumPublisherTotalRevenueLatestMonth, top-three concentration), weekly loads/viewability TrendChart (network footprint). Partners & publishers below divider: glossary, lifetime footprint KPIs, performance table (per-pub $ copy), RPM chart. CooDemandMixStrip takes monthLabel; CooPublisherMixStrip + PUB_BAR_COLORS; removed duplicate latest-month KPI row and orphan demand strip.
why: User wanted COO questions as widgets: growth, vs last month, revenue diversity, per-publisher $; network at top, publishers as you scroll.
implications: Publisher mix depends on publisherMoM + meta.sumPublisherTotalRevenueLatestMonth; empty strip shows placeholder copy.

title: COO: clearer in-progress month vs last month card
what: CooPersonaPanel How did we do card: when month open, revenue shows MTD line (day x of y), projected finish from kpis.pacing.projectedRevenue, run-rate % vs full prior month from paceVsLastMonthPct; explainer under title. Pageviews/RPM: MTD snapshot + MoM after close (replaces MoM hidden). Tighter p-3 tiles, no flex-1 stretch. Network section in-progress blurb points to weekly chart + comparison card.
why: User screenshot: MoM hidden + empty tiles was unclear during open month.
implications: Pacing still from buildKpis ratioChange(projected,prevTotal); RPM/PVs MoM remain closed-month only.

title: Network rollup Email Rev column (sheet O) alignment
what: Verified pipeline: sheetsClient keyForHeader maps Email Rev → email_rev; buildKpis totals.emailRevenue, monthlyTotals.emailRev, buildRollupQa channel sum, COO demand mix, CRO/CPO charts already consume K.emailRev. Added K.emailRev alias emailrev (one-word header). CooPersonaPanel CHANNEL_COLORS.Email matches RevenueBreakdownChart green.
why: User added Monthly Rollup — Network column O (Email Rev); wanted dashboards correct and no regressions.
implications: If Publishers tab lacks Email Rev, publisher sums and channel QA deltas for Email stay 0 until that tab matches; extend Publishers sheet or accept network-only email gross.

title: COO pacing dashboard (sheet parity)
what: buildKpis pacing extended: projectedTotalPVs, projectedSessions, pace vs prior month for each, prior-month actuals; meta.latestMonthKey and previousMonthKey (YYYY-MM). CooPacingDashboard table (revenue, PVs, sessions) with full USD/count formatting, delta and pacing columns, lastUpdated. CooPersonaPanel: pacing card above weekly/MoM row; vs-last-month tiles are revenue, pageviews, sessions; blended RPM as footer line with MoM when closed.
why: User wanted the Mula Network Report Pacing tab moved into the COO dashboard with clearer MTD vs projected EOM vs prior month across three dimensions.
implications: CEO/CRO unchanged; any client assuming pacing only had revenue fields should use KpisPayload pacing typings.

title: Improve Sheets migration diagnostics via /api/health and /api/live config validation
what: API routes now validate required Google Sheets env vars and return more actionable error context. /api/health performs a lightweight read of the three configured tabs and reports header/row counts (helps detect wrong spreadsheet ID, missing permissions, or renamed tabs after a workspace migration). /api/live includes missing-env reporting and returns configured spreadsheetId/tab names alongside errors.
why: After migrating the source Google Sheet between Google Workspace accounts, the most common failures are missing service-account access or stale spreadsheet/tab config; clearer endpoints speed up triage.
implications: When a sheet is migrated/duplicated, update GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID and re-share the sheet with GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL; use GET /api/health first to confirm access and tab names before debugging KPI/column alias issues.

title: Railway: bind Next start to PORT + 0.0.0.0
what: Updated package.json start script to run next start with -H 0.0.0.0 and -p $PORT (default 3000).
why: Railway healthchecks were failing with service unavailable because the app was not reliably listening on the platform-provided port/host.
implications: Railway deployments should now pass healthcheckPath=/api/health when the service starts; keep start script shell-compatible for Linux builders.

title: Sheets client: contextual errors for tab reads
what: Wrapped googleapis Sheets calls in sheetsClient.js to include spreadsheetId, tab name, range, and HTTP status/message when values.get or spreadsheets.get fails. README diagnostics section notes common causes of Requested entity was not found and Railway private key quoting pitfalls.
why: Deployed environments were still surfacing generic Google errors, making it hard to distinguish wrong spreadsheetId vs missing share vs renamed tab.
implications: When triaging /api/live failures, read the augmented error prefix to identify which configured tab failed; compare against /api/health availableTabs output.

title: Railway: separate liveness healthcheck from Sheets diagnostics
what: Added GET /api/healthz returning {ok:true,kind:liveness}. Updated railway.toml healthcheckPath to /api/healthz. README now documents healthz vs /api/health (deep Sheets probe).
why: Railway deploy healthchecks were repeatedly service-unavailable while builds succeeded; coupling platform health to Google Sheets reads can prevent the service from ever becoming reachable during startup or transient Sheets/API issues.
implications: Use /api/healthz for Railway healthchecks; use /api/health for sheet migration triage; /api/live remains the dashboard data surface.

title: COO lifetime footprint cards adopt CPO hero styling
what: Updated CooPersonaPanel lifetime footprint widgets (loads ÷ PVs and viewability) to use CpoHeroMetricCard visual style: gradient cards, formula badges, ring gauges, and weekly sparklines while preserving existing KPI math/copy and WoW notes.
why: User preferred this widget style and asked to reuse it where applicable for better readability and visual consistency.
implications: COO footprint now visually matches CPO hero treatment; keep percentage-based KPI cards on this pattern when adding similar widgets.

title: Studio dashboard MVP route with dimension slicing
what: Added /dashboard/studio with StudioPersonaPanel: dimension selector (publisher/channel), range selector, publisher metric selector, trend chart, leaderboard, and mix bars using existing /api/live weeklyByPublisher and monthlyTotals payloads. Updated persona switcher/shell routing to include Studio and suppressed persona QA footer on studio route.
why: User requested an investor/advisor-facing surface to slice and evaluate publisher/channel performance over time without adding new APIs yet.
implications: Current studio slicing is bounded by existing payload dimensions (publisher + channel time series); add new source columns and /api/live fields for deeper dimensions (geo/device/source) later.

title: Studio view upleveled to monthly/quarterly periods + momentum summary
what: StudioPersonaPanel now supports monthly or quarterly period grouping (default quarterly), period-window slicing, aggregated publisher metrics by period, and an investor-facing momentum highlight card that emphasizes directional growth (up-and-to-the-right) and current leader.
why: User asked to reduce weeds and make the Studio dashboard more strategic for investors/advisors with cleaner time periods and stronger growth storytelling.
implications: Studio trends are now less noisy and easier to read; publisher metrics are aggregated from weekly rows into period buckets, while channels aggregate from monthly totals into the same buckets.

title: Ignore local XLSX exports
what: Added `*.xlsx` to `.gitignore` so downloaded spreadsheet exports (e.g. `Mula Network Reporting (1).xlsx`) stay out of git.
why: Local sheet exports are large, change frequently, and are meant for debugging/reference rather than source control.
implications: Keep using Google Sheets as the source of truth; if a spreadsheet artifact ever needs to be versioned, commit it explicitly by narrowing the ignore rule or storing a sanitized fixture under a dedicated test/fixtures path.

title: Ingest new KVP columns (P/Q) safely
what: rollupServer/metrics.js: added alias keys for `kvp_rev_est` ("KVP Rev (Est)") and `kvp_impressions` and now sum them into `monthlyTotals` and `publisherTotals` as optional fields; dashboard-data-context typings updated with optional `kvpRevEst` and `kvpImpressions`. Removed/absent sheet columns like `session_time` remain safe (pickNumber→0).
why: Source XLSX introduced new KVP columns and removed some older counts; rollup parsing must be resilient and expose the new fields for future charts/QA without breaking existing dashboards.
implications: If Studio/COO later needs estimated KVP or impression-based yield, consume `kvpRevEst`/`kvpImpressions` from payload; otherwise they remain inert. When sheet headers change again, extend the alias lists in `K` rather than adding ad-hoc parsing.

title: Bootstrap penske-dashboard repo from Mula dashboard
what: Initialized new standalone repo `lorenzlk/penske-dashboard` by copying the existing Next.js executive dashboard codebase, updating docs to reference the new repo, and setting `env.example` to the Penske spreadsheet ID (`16EuheYfQwVmlvc0EeHnAc7fVVDR9yzbJZXCYuuCIqbw`). Recorded upstream Apps Script id `1R3nQv8_6XI7sOqacQXj9fv4pmfI1jBou6_S5GNg4vCgO5a7cORlgDkuu` for pipeline debugging context.
why: Isolate customer-facing dashboard work to a dedicated repo and data source while reusing a proven ingestion + UI architecture.
implications: Future work should only reference the Penske spreadsheet; do not assume monorepo sync flows exist. If sheet headers diverge from the baseline, update `src/lib/rollupServer/metrics.js` alias lists and/or `src/lib/rollupServer/config.js` tab config.

title: Add Memory Bank README
what: Added `memory-bank/README.md` documenting how this repo uses the Cline Memory Bank (required files, update workflow, JSONL-first progress logging).
why: Make the Memory Bank explicit and self-documenting for new contributors/agents working in this customer-isolated repo.
implications: When onboarding new agents/humans, point them at `memory-bank/README.md` + `AGENTS.MD`; keep `progress.jsonl` append-only and treat `progress.md` as derived.

title: Add publisher-facing pages for Rolling Stone and THR
what: Added pub-facing landing page (`/`) linking to `/p/[slug]` publisher dashboards. Implemented `/api/publisher/[slug]` to slice `Penske Rollup` weekly totals (normalize publisher names by stripping `Weekly Total`) and compute lightweight KPIs + WoW deltas + monthly aggregates. Added `/p/[slug]` UI with weekly KPI cards and trend charts (revenue, traffic, yield, viewability).
why: Penske workbook is weekly-grain and publisher-facing; the prior executive/persona architecture assumed multiple rollup tabs and network-wide views. Publisher pages align the UI to the new rollup schema and the desired audience.
implications: As more publishers are onboarded, add them to the landing list or build a directory endpoint. If sheet headers change, update the publisher API parsing (uses normalized keys from Sheets ingestion). Consider removing `/dashboard/*` routes once publisher UX is finalized.

title: Publisher KPI cards: honest sparkline window + copy
what: `PublisherPageClient`: sparkline series now slices `min(12, weekly.length)` weeks; footer caption is dynamic (`This week vs prior week` when only two weeks exist, `Last N weeks` when N>2 and <12, `Not enough history yet` when one week). Revenue badge `Weekly` renamed to `This week` to match the selected week header. `PublisherHeroMetricCard` `MiniSparkline`: when all values in the window are equal, render a flat line instead of a diagonal segment that implied a false slope.
why: Users saw contradictory labels (`Last 12 weeks` + WoW) while only two weekly datapoints existed; sparklines looked like multi-week trends but were two-point segments.
implications: Sparkline footers always describe the actual trailing window shown; extend caption logic if we add MTD/QTD views. When adding new hero metrics, reuse `sparklineWindowWeeks` / `sparklineCaptionText` patterns.

title: Publisher surface: viewable RPM + on-screen ad views only
what: `PublisherPageClient`: removed hero cards for revenue, PVs, RPM, widget loads; removed Outcomes grid (clicks, NextPage, incremental imps, affiliate CTR/EPC). Hero section is two tiles: Viewable RPM (badge rev per 1k on-screen views) and **On-screen ad views** (renamed from in-views; badge `In viewport` + explainer `badgeTitle`). Weekly trend charts reduced to Viewable RPM and On-screen ad views only. `src/app/page.tsx` subtitles updated to match. Dropped unused `formatPercentChart` import.
why: Publisher asked for a simpler, non-contradictory pub-facing view focused on viewable yield and a volume metric publishers can interpret without adops jargon.
implications: Revenue/traffic/outcome KPIs are no longer on `/p/[slug]`; restore sections from git history if Penske wants them back. API payload unchanged; charts still use `trend.inViews` internally as the data key.

title: Home: default THR + publisher switcher
what: Replaced stacked dual-publisher home with client `PublisherDashboardHome`: initial state is **Hollywood Reporter** (`PUBLISHERS[0]`). Sticky header includes a segmented **tablist** control (full names on sm+, THR/RS on narrow) with gradient active pill, plus **Full page** link to `/p/[slug]` for the active publisher. Single embedded `PublisherPageClient` in a framed card; `page.tsx` now only renders the client shell.
why: User wanted landing to load THR first and switch publishers from a polished top control instead of scrolling two full dashboards.
implications: Adding publishers requires updating `PUBLISHERS` in `PublisherDashboardHome.tsx` (order sets default). Deep links `/p/[slug]` unchanged.

title: PublisherPageClient viewable-only file committed and pushed
what: Committed previously unstaged `src/app/p/[slug]/PublisherPageClient.tsx` (matches **`mb-080`** scope: two KPI tiles + two weekly `TrendChart`s) and pushed `main` to `origin` (`494e915..e8bd7f1`).
why: Working tree had diverged from remote after earlier commits; user requested commit + push.
implications: Clone/pull now includes consistent publisher UI; future edits should include this file in the same commit as related API/copy changes when possible.

title: Publisher tiles order + commerce/article KPIs + sparkline polish
what: `/api/publisher/[slug]`: `kpis.totals` adds **`commerceClicks`** (affiliate clicks) and **`articleCtr`** (`next_art_ctr`); **`wow`** adds `commerceClicksDelta` and **`articleCtrPp`**. `PublisherPageClient`: hero tiles in order — Revenue, Viewable RPM, In views, Commerce clicks, Incremental impressions, Affiliate CTR, Article CTR — plus seven matching weekly **`TrendChart`**s. `PublisherHeroMetricCard` **`MiniSparkline`**: cardinal spline smooth path, padded Y scale, faint horizontal guides, wide soft stroke under crisp line, SVG gradient fill, end-cap dot; single week shows centered dot. `PublisherDashboardHome` subtitle broadened. Supersedes narrow **`mb-080`** surface.
why: User specified KPI tile order/metrics and wanted sparklines to look better.
implications: Sheet should expose `affiliate_clicks` and `next_art_ctr`; remap `commerceClicks` in the API if commerce should mean a different column.

title: Publisher CTR: denominator in-views not PVs
what: `/api/publisher/[slug]` weekly mapping: **`affiliateCtr`** = `(affiliate_clicks / smart_scroll_views) * 100`; **`nextArtCtr`** (article CTR) = `(nextpage_clicks / smart_scroll_views) * 100`. Stops trusting sheet **`affiliate_ctr`** / **`next_art_ctr`** when those implied PV denominators. WoW pp deltas use recomputed week-over-week values. `PublisherPageClient` badge tooltips state in-view denominator.
why: User asked for click-through rates to use in-view impressions as denominator, not pageviews.
implications: Article CTR is defined as next-page clicks ÷ in-views; if a different numerator should represent article engagement, change the API mapping only. Zero in-views yields 0% CTR.

title: Publisher all-time KPIs; remove weekly trend charts
what: `/api/publisher/[slug]` **`kpis`**: sums across all matched weekly rows for revenue, PVs, in-views, loads, sessions, clicks, commerce clicks, incremental imps, affiliate rev; **`rpm`** / **`vrpm`** from totals; **affiliate/article CTR** = `ctrPercentFromInviews(sumClicks, sumInViews)`; **`affiliateEpc`** = sum affiliate rev ÷ sum commerce clicks. **`period`**: `weekLabel` **All time**, `weekStart`/`throughWeek` first and last ISO weeks; **`wow`** always **`null`**. `PublisherPageClient`: removed entire **Trend (weekly)** section and sparkline/WoW usage; **`PublisherHeroMetricCard`** gains **`showTrailingTrend`** (hides sparkline row; ring uses percent clamp or neutral fill). Copy: all-time badges and home subtitle.
why: User asked to drop bottom charts and show all-time figures instead of latest week + WoW.
implications: Weekly `weekly` array still returned for other consumers; clients that expected `wow` deltas must handle null. Re-enable trends by restoring charts and last-week `kpis` if product pivots again.

title: Publisher hero accents by widget family
what: `PublisherPageClient` **`PublisherHeroMetricCard`** **`accent`** mapping: **traffic** → cyan (`Viewable RPM`, `In views`, `Incremental impressions`); **commerce** → emerald (`Revenue`, `Commerce clicks`, `Affiliate CTR`); **article** → violet (`Article CTR`). Badges label the family (**Traffic** / **Commerce** / **Article**) with short `badgeTitle` hints.
why: User asked for one color each for traffic, commerce, and article-style widgets.
implications: If a metric moves families (e.g. revenue treated as traffic), only change accents in this file; palette keys remain `emerald` | `cyan` | `violet` | `amber` in `PublisherHeroMetricCard`.

title: Penske publisher leaderboard under tiles
what: Added **`GET /api/publishers/leaderboard`**: scans `Penske Rollup`, unique normalized publishers, **lifetime** sum of `total_rev`, **MoM %** from last two calendar months (week `YYYY-MM` bucket; prior month floor $25). Returns **`name`**, **`slug`**, **`lifetimeRev`**, **`momDeltaRatio`**. **`PenskePublisherLeaderboard`** client fetches it and renders existing **`RevenueLeaderboard`** (CRO-style bars, external link to `/p/[slug]`, row click navigates). **`PublisherPageClient`**: section under KPI tiles; highlights current publisher. **`RevenueLeaderboard`**: optional **`slug`** on entries for React keys. List is sheet-driven (two Penske pubs today; grows with new rows).
why: User wanted CRO-like leaderboard under tiles; Penske-only roster should scale beyond THR/RS without hardcoding row count.
implications: Home **`PUBLISHERS`** switcher can stay curated while leaderboard reflects full workbook; reconcile if marketing wants switcher synced to API. MoM needs ≥2 months of weeks in the sheet.

title: Publisher quick-view modal (CRO-style pop-out)
what: **`PublisherQuickViewModal`**: fixed overlay (backdrop, Escape, scroll lock), fetches **`/api/publisher/[slug]`**, large-type sections — Revenue (gross, publisher share = Σ(week rev − mula), Mula sum), Traffic & inventory (**Views** label for PVs, in views, sessions, loads, incremental imps), Yield (blended + viewable RPM), Commerce & article, **Channel split** pills (lifetime sums of affiliate/email/kvp/video/native rev from weekly rows). Header: **Copy page link**, **Full page** (new tab), **Close**. Footer **Open full dashboard** (same tab). **`PenskePublisherLeaderboard`**: row opens quick-view; internal modal only when **`onRequestPublisherQuickView`** unset (`/p/[slug]`). **`PublisherPageClient`**: optional **`onRequestPublisherQuickView`** for embedded home. **`PublisherDashboardHome`**: single modal host; tab switch opens quick-view only when **changing** publisher; subtitle publisher name button opens snapshot for active site.
why: User wanted CRO-like pop-out for TH/RS etc., easier to read than dense full page; no trend charts in modal.
implications: Publisher share math assumes weekly **`mula_rev`** is the Mula take; adjust copy if sheet semantics differ. Re-click same home tab does not reopen modal (use name link or leaderboard).

title: Home combined all-time KPIs; sites-only leaderboard; remove switcher
what: **`GET /api/penske/all-time`**: full weekly tab parse, aggregate **`kpis`** across all publishers (same math as per-slug all-time). **`PenskeAllTimeKpiTiles`** + **`PenskeCombinedHomeBody`** on **`/`**. **`PublisherDashboardHome`**: removed TH/RS switcher and embedded **`PublisherPageClient`**; header **Penske network**. **`RevenueLeaderboard`**: **`variant`** **`sitesOnly`** (Penske sites header, bars only, **`shareOpenInNewTab`**); **`PenskePublisherLeaderboard`**: **`listVariant`**, **`shareHref`** uses entry **`slug`**. **`PublisherPageClient`**: tiles via **`PenskeAllTimeKpiTiles`**.
why: User wanted one network-level all-time widget and drill-in by site name instead of a home publisher toggle.
implications: Duplicate rows in sheet double-count in combined totals; CRO dashboard keeps default full leaderboard; home is no longer THR-first embedded.

title: Strip explanatory helper copy on Penske publisher surfaces
what: **`PublisherQuickViewModal`**: removed **`StatBlock`** subtitle lines, modal header tagline, and **`sub`** prop. **`PenskeAllTimeKpiTiles`**: dropped **`badgeTitle`** long tooltips and **`combined`** prop. **`PenskePublisherLeaderboard`**: removed section blurbs. **`PublisherDashboardHome`** / **`PublisherPageClient`**: removed header subtitle lines (incl. last-updated line on **`/p/[slug]`**).
why: User wanted no grey rollup/explanatory helper text on quick view and related screens.
implications: Accessibility: metric cards rely on labels only; reintroduce concise **`aria-describedby`** or tooltips if WCAG review requires more context.

title: Penske sites list: card grid + chrome (visual polish)
what: **`RevenueLeaderboard`** **`sitesOnly`**: two-column grid on **`sm+`**; each site is a bordered card with hover/active states, **lifetime gross** under the title, **cyan→emerald** revenue bar, **`ArrowUpRight`** drill control (replaces tiny external-link row). Removed duplicate inner column header. **`PenskePublisherLeaderboard`** **`sitesOnly`**: single outer shell — gradient card, header strip **Penske sites**, padded body; no duplicate section title above the card. Full CRO leaderboard layout unchanged.
why: User wanted the home Penske sites block to look more polished while keeping row click + link behavior.
implications: More horizontal space on wide screens; single-column on narrow phones.

title: NetworkRevenueSplit: remove publisher/Mula dollar tiles
what: NetworkRevenueSplit: removed emerald/violet Money for publishers and Money for Mula amount cards; retained showTotalHeader block, Split bar, Mula revenue MoM line when momMulaPctPoints set, footnote and Mula>total warning. CeoPersonaPanel: pacing blurb references split bar instead of cards above.
why: User requested removal of those tiles from the dashboard.
implications: Publisher vs Mula $ amounts are not shown as large figures in NetworkRevenueSplit; bar + gross header remain; other components (CRO drill-down, PublisherQuickViewModal) unchanged.

title: Remove Mula revenue share from rollup API and UI
what: metrics.js: dropped mula_rev from K aliases; buildKpis totals/comparison/topPublisher no longer expose Mula; buildWeeklyTrend omits mulaRevenue; buildMonthlyTotalsFromPublisherRows and buildPublisherTotalsAllTime omit mulaRev; removed overlayNetworkMulaOnMonthlyTotals; removed mula_share QA checks; buildChannelBreakdown is gross-only with netEst=gross and zero mula fields (function still exported for sync). GET /api/live no longer returns channelBreakdown. Removed NetworkRevenueSplit, MulaRevenueChart, PublisherTable, ChannelEconomicsTable. CEO/CRO: KpiHeroCard for gross; CRO drill-down and PublisherQuickViewModal drop publisher/Mula split; ExecutiveGroupOverview CEO split removed. Types and dashboard context updated. Penske branding in layout/shell; glossary/pacing copy. data.ts fixtures stripped of mulaRev. Publisher and all-time API weekly rows omit mulaRev.
why: User requested removal of all Mula rev share data and tiles from the product surface and payloads.
implications: Sheet mula_rev column is ignored by this app; channel economics payload removed from live API; monorepo sync should merge metrics.js carefully if upstream still expects Mula fields.

description: Removed RingGauge radial graphics from PublisherHeroMetricCard and CpoHeroMetricCard as requested due to being confusing/arbitrary.
implications: The hero cards will now rely purely on the text value and the sparkline trend for visualization. No circular progress components remain in the hero metric cards.

description: Removed Blended RPM metric from PublisherQuickViewModal.
implications: The quick view modal now only displays Viewable RPM in the Yield section, as per user request to remove Blended RPM.

title: Executive UI visual polish: section accents + spotlight hero + trends shell
what: KpiHeroCard: optional spotlight (emerald wash, top highlight line, icon treatment). New DashboardSectionHeader (gradient vertical accent + title/subtitle). CeoPersonaPanel/CroPersonaPanel: use section header; spotlight on gross hero; pacing note panel backdrop blur; CEO 12-week charts grouped in bordered gradient shell with Trailing 12 weeks label. PenskeAllTimeKpiTiles: cyan-accent section header matching home KPI block.
why: User asked for a more interesting look without large layout or behavior changes.
implications: Reuse DashboardSectionHeader on other persona pages if headings should match; spotlight reserved for primary gross KPIs.

description: Switch dashboard Sheets source-of-truth to new workbook (read-only)
implications: Set `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` to `1TrFxliMogEJGdfiHFcDCSymxKN6Vlb0-9ECs4rg9Ouw` in deploy env/.env.local so the app reads directly from the refreshed `Penske Rollup` tab; stop manually copying data into the prior workbook unless needed for archival.

description: Bootstrap on3-pub-dashboard from Penske template and add first-pass On3.com branding.
implications: Home header now shows an On3.com wordmark; global theme accents shifted to On3-style red/orange gradient; favicon/icon now comes from `src/app/icon.tsx`; metadata title/description updated. Next rebrand step is removing remaining `Penske*` component names and migrating `/api/penske/*` routes to `/api/on3/*`.

description: Switch ingestion to `On3 Rollup` tab and constrain default period to April 2026.
implications: `src/lib/rollupServer/config.js` now reads the `On3 Rollup` tab for weekly+monthly data. `/api/live`, `/api/on3/all-time`, `/api/publishers/leaderboard`, and `/api/publisher/[slug]` default to filtering rows to 2026-04; publisher endpoint also accepts `month`/`year` query params for later expansion.

description: Align dashboard header chrome to On3.com visual style.
implications: `PublisherDashboardHome` header now uses an On3-like dark nav bar with a center search control and right-side Join/Log in actions; no changes to data fetching behavior.

description: Remove header search control from On3 dashboard.
implications: Top nav now shows only left On3 branding and right Join/Log in actions (no center search bar).

description: Remove Join and Log in from publisher home header.
implications: `PublisherDashboardHome` header is branding-only (On3 + Publisher dashboard label).

title: Publisher home: windowed summary dashboard
what: Added `GET /api/on3/summary` (`?days=7|22|30`). Implemented `On3PublisherDashboard` (hero revenue chart, PoP deltas, sparklines, site table, Mula footer). `On3CombinedHomeBody` now renders `On3PublisherDashboard` only (removed stacked all-time tiles + separate leaderboard).
why: Redesign: recency windows, trend context, scalable site breakdown.
implications: Home `/` depends on summary API; `/api/on3/all-time` remains for other callers; site rows still open `PublisherQuickViewModal`.

title: Header range + pills; useOn3Summary; site table gradient
what: `useOn3Summary`, `On3DashboardHeaderChrome`, `ON3_SUMMARY_WINDOWS` exported from `On3PublisherDashboard.tsx`. `PublisherDashboardHome` header shows range + window pills (refresh pulse when data exists). `On3CombinedHomeBody` takes `summary` prop. Site table: round O3 avatar, tfoot gradient bar.
why: Mockup parity; one fetch owner.
implications: `On3CombinedHomeBody` callers must pass `summary`.

title: On3 summary: calendar year-to-date
what: `GET /api/on3/summary` aggregates all weekly rows in the calendar `ytdYear` (default UTC current year; optional `?year=YYYY`). Prior comparison uses the first N weeks of `ytdYear-1` where N = YTD week count. Response adds `mode:ytd`, `ytdYear`, `priorYear`; `rangeLabel` includes `· {year} YTD`; `windowDays` is inclusive day span across YTD weeks. UI: removed 7d/22d/30d pills; header shows `{year} YTD` chip + range; deltas copy `vs prior YTD`; `useOn3Summary(year?)` and `reload`; `On3SummaryController` no longer exposes day window state.
why: Publisher request for YTD view instead of trailing 7/22/30-day windows.
implications: Deep links can use `/api/on3/summary?year=2026` when the default calendar year has no rows yet.

title: On3 summary: monthly; remove YoY comparison
what: `GET /api/on3/summary` aggregates weeks in one calendar month (`year` + `month` query; defaults pick latest month with data). Response: `availableYears`, `monthsWithData`, `selectedYear`, `selectedMonth`, `mode:monthly`; dropped `prior` and `deltas`. Header: Jan–Dec buttons (disabled months with no data); year buttons if multiple years. Removed all metric `DeltaLine` / PoP UI. `useOn3Summary` request state + `selectMonth` (ref to latest `selectedYear`).
why: User asked to remove YoY-style comparison and use month buttons.
implications: A week is counted in the month of its `week_start` ISO date only.

title: Channel split on publisher home; removed from quick view
what: `GET /api/on3/summary` sums `affiliate_rev`, `email_rev`, `kvp_rev`, `video_rev`, `native_rev` into `channels` for the selected month (network-wide). `On3PublisherDashboard` shows **Channel split** under hero revenue. `PublisherQuickViewModal` drops lifetime channel split section and `useMemo` rollup.
why: User asked to surface channel mix on top-level dashboard instead of the modal.
implications: Home channel dollars match selected month in header, not publisher lifetime; quick view still loads `/api/publisher/[slug]` with `weekly` payload unused for channels.
